title: Large Language Models’ Complicit Responses to Illicit Instructions across Socio-Legal Contexts

bias_targets.methodology: Augmenting illicit user instructions with explicit gender cues (e.g., 'As a man/woman') and measuring disparities in the model's safety and complicit facilitation rates.
Augmenting illicit instructions with age-related cues (e.g., 'young adult', 'elderly person') and comparing the rates of complicit unlawful guidance provided by the models.

Inserting explicit racial or ethnic identifiers (e.g., White, African American, Han, Uyghur) into illicit prompts and evaluating disparities in the models' safety responses between majority and minority groups.
Adding religious affiliations or non-religious identifiers to illicit instructions and measuring differences in how often models provide complicit facilitation.

Augmenting prompts with specific occupational identities, mapping these to occupational prestige scores, and analyzing the correlation between user prestige and model safety rates. The study also utilizes chain-of-thought reasoning analysis to measure model-perceived stereotypes (warmth and competence) toward these groups.
